questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to explore a new city and country, without compromising with the academic level. I specifically applied for Universität Mannheim because it is has a high ranking within social science and the location is really attractive. The city is 'only' around the size of Aarhus and the architecture is nothing to write home about. But it is beatifully located between the rivers Rhine and Neckar and has good transport opportunities to other large cities and great nature experiences. For me, it was very important   to be somewhere that was different from Copenhagen and Mannheim was perfect for that.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I would rate my stay a 9, because I had an amazing experience, but I was affected a little bit by COVID restrictions. Nothing too severe though, and it was never really a problem.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The university webpage can be messy, but with time I was able too look up everything I needed to know. The university's international office is very good at sending informing email. But be patient, things works slower in Germany.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The international office and the economics department held several Zoom meetings before semester start. This was very nice.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
The university offers housing at different dorms. If you choose this, just be aware that some of them are located in the city center and other quit far from the campus.
I found housing on my own, because I preferred living in a small shared flat. I found my room on
wg-gesucht.de
, which is a great webside for finding rooms or small apartments. I had the best time with my two german roomies, and was very glad to live with locals.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Be aware of the distance to campus. I lived in the middle of the Quadrate, so everything was in walking distance for me. If you find something further away you have transport option. There are city bikes all over the city which offers the first 30min free of charge for students. You can also get a semester ticket for the trams.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Apply well in advanced. I started my room search in May, even though the semester doesn't begin before September.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
This is unlike anything we are used to from UCPH. The registration begins just before the semester begins. This implies that you application and pre-approval process is based on last years course catalog and there can be changes very close to the beginning of the semester. At the university it is possible to try out classes before you decides what to take. Only a few of them require an early registration.
This stressed my, because we are used to something else from Copenhagen. However everything worked out fine in the end and I was able to get all the courses I wanted.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
The course catalog is released some time in during the summer holidays. It contain all information you need. You sign up for courses through the univerisyt platform Portal2.
The exam registration comes later, some time in the middle of the semester. The university does not release the exam dates with the course catalog, these come later. However the university guarantees that no exams overlap as long as you stick with courses from the same department.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The webside offers some guidance, but I would suggest to ask another student for help if you need it.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses that I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take a breath when you get frustrated with how late the course information is released. You will manage everything in time, no problem.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Be aware that written exam are done by hand. The university is not very good at informing us digitalized students from the north about this.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I found the level very similar to what I am used to. At least it was not more difficult than at UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
There is mostly only lectures and the few exercise classes I had were focused on student presentations. 
The grading is different, in most of my courses my final grade was made up of in-class presentations, assignment and a final exam. I really liked this, because it reduced my stress at the final examination, because at had already passed some of the class. 
I made more presentations than usually. I think I did 6 in total. But I only had one home assignment during the semester.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Banking and bank regulation (5 ECTS), Economic and financial market policy (5 ECTS), Chinese economy (5 ECTS), Poverty and inequality (7 ECTS), Health economics (7 ECTS)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I really enjoyed 'economic and financial market policy'. The course had some theory, but was mainly focused on current issues. We also did a case presentation where we where asked to find information on and present our own solutions to issues. 
'Chinese economy' was interesting because UCPH does not offer something like it. The professor was super motivated and was very open to question we had and giving advice on our exam-report. 
'Poverty and inequalty' brought new perspectives on the subject, which was super interesting.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: You have to pay an initial fee to the university. Also you also pay a broadcasting fee in Germany. This is approx. 18€ a month.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food, drinks and rent are much cheaper than Copenhagen. You can by lunch in the university cafeteria or around the city for 3-5 euros. Public transportation is as expensive as in Copenhagen. If you travel to larger cities with the ICE trains might even be more expensive. With the student card you can travel for free in the local area after 7pm and in the weekends. I used this a lot to explore the area around the Mannheim.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There is a sports club through the university. The offer a wide range of different sports. I went to some of their yoga classes, which were really nice. 
There is also a crazy long list of different student organizations. Take a look and show up for the ones you find interesting. I participated in some events from AEGEE Mannheim, which was great.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Take part in the exchange student events arranged by ESN VISUM Mannheim. This is great way to meet other internationals. Sign up for the buddy program. Your buddy is a local student, who knows the city and the university.
I like to swim, so I went a lot to the pool Herschelbad.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Visit cities like Heidelberg, Speyer, Frankfurt and Weinheim. Go hiking in the hills behind Heidelberg or Neustadt, the views are amazing. Do a wine-hike, the area is big on wine production, especially Riesling. If you go in fall, then definitely visit Christmas markets and drink glühwein.
Watch a handball- or icehockey game. The two teams in Mannheim both play in the best german league.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Even more if you know some basic german. Most older germans and even some students are not very good in english.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to all the erasmus events, do not be scared to show up alone, many others are in the same boat as you.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Remeber to always have cash on hand. You can pay with card in supermarkets and larger stores, but at restaurants and bars, cash is the way to go.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I only met super friendly and open people. Everywhere I went people were so nice and invited me along to the things they did.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Remeber to enjoy your stay. Exchange is so much more than just academia. Go hiking, get beer in Jungbusch and have a coffee at the rivers.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Train is cheaper than flying. If you can overcome the long travel time, this is the easiest way to arrive.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The amazing people I met. I am definitely going back to visit them.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The practical stuff with the university. But this was a small thing compared to the entire stay.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Don't dicard Mannheim just because you do not know the city. It is a student city filled with great people who will make sure you get the best stay possible.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
